- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizons.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% for 3–7 day horizons.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 1–2 days); apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 10–20% for 3–5 day horizons following spikes.
- Mean reversion is evident in 7–14 day horizons: if forecast is > 2σ above recent mean, reduce by 5–15% for next 3–7 days.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33) triggers downward bias; reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 10+ day horizons, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply “smooth decay” — reduce forecast by 2–5% per additional day beyond 7.
